what.text: This page follows refugees from Sudan living in the Central African Republic, as counted by UNHCR at the end of each year.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 40204 Sudanese refugees there, 1.4% of all refugees from Sudan.
Chad hosts the most Sudanese refugees, followed by South Sudan, Libya and Ethiopia.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over Southern Sudan territory from 1963 to 1972 and over the government of Sudan from 1983 to 2018, at war level in many years.
From 2020 to 2025 it records armed conflict over the government of Sudan with the SLM/A, RSF, SPLM/A-North and SFA.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 1964 at 300 refugees.
The main years of displacement in the data are 1966 to 1967, 1970 to 1971, 1993 to 2003 and 2023 to 2025, and the figure is at its highest at the end of 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in the Central African Republic.
These are year-end totals for the Central African Republic only, reported to UNHCR.
